title: Potential dualizing complexes with prime-power coefficients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $T$ a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; excellent means that its affine coordinate rings are excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use the small etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Put $\Lambda_T(1)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}$, the sheaf of units with $u^{\ell^n}=1$, with its $\Lambda$-module structure by exponentiation [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Positive twists are tensor powers, the zeroth twist is $\Lambda_T$, and negative twists are dual powers [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-sheaf]. On complexes put $M(a)=M\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda_T(a)$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], with cohomological shifts $[b]$. Use the signed twist and root-of-unity inverse-image identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback].

For a geometric point $\bar x$ above $x\in T$ write $T_{(\bar x)}$ for the strict localization [def-weil-geometric-point], [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. A geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ is a $T$-map $T_{(\bar y)}\to T_{(\bar x)}$. It is immediate if the reduced closure of the image of $\bar y$ in $T_{(\bar x)}$ has Krull dimension one, where Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets. A dimension function is $\delta:|T|\to\mathbf Z$ satisfying $\delta(y)=\delta(x)+1$ at every immediate geometric specialization.

For a closed immersion $i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with complementary open $j$, write $i^!$ for the right derived functor on $\Lambda$-module sheaves of $i^{-1}\ker(1\to j_*j^{-1})$ [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. For a point $x$ define $R\Gamma_xK=i_x^!(K|_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,x}})$ in $D^+(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, where $i_x$ is the closed-point inclusion and $\kappa(x)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. At $\bar x$ take its geometric fibre $R\Gamma_{\bar x}K=(R\Gamma_xK)_{\bar x}$. Its natural identification with supported cohomology on $T_{(\bar x)}$ [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections] is supplied by [lem-per-prime-power-costalk-reduction].

A pinned potential dualizing complex for $(T,\delta,\Lambda)$ consists of $K\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and, for every $x\in T$, an isomorphism on the residue-field etale site
$$p_x:R\Gamma_xK\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(\delta(x))[2\delta(x)],$$
satisfying, for every immediate geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$, the equality in $D^+(\Lambda)$
$$p_{\bar y}=p_{\bar x}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}:R\Gamma_{\bar y}K\longrightarrow\Lambda(\delta(y))[2\delta(y)].$$
Here $p_{\bar z}$ is the geometric fibre of $p_z$. The target of $p_{\bar x}(1)[2]$ is identified by the signed twist tensor/evaluation identifications and transport of roots of unity along the specified geometric specialization as
$$\bigl(\Lambda(\delta(x))[2\delta(x)]\bigr)(1)[2]\simeq\Lambda(\delta(x)+1)[2\delta(x)+2]=\Lambda(\delta(y))[2\delta(y)].$$

The fixed normalized residue transition is constructed as follows. In $T_{(\bar x)}$, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T_{(\bar x)}$ be the reduced closure of the image of $\bar y$, set $L=i^!(K|_{T_{(\bar x)}})$, and take the normalization $\nu:\widetilde Z\to Z$ [def-sc-normalization]. By [lem-per-prime-power-costalk-reduction], $\widetilde Z$ is a strictly henselian trait (the spectrum of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]) and $d=[\kappa(\widetilde z_0):\kappa(z_0)]$ is invertible in $\Lambda$, for their closed points $z_0,\widetilde z_0$. Set
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}=d^{-1}\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde Z}(\nu^*L)$$
under that lemma's identifications of $R\Gamma_{\bar y}K$ with $(\nu^*L)_{\bar\eta}$ and of $R\Gamma_{\bar x}K$ with $R\Gamma_{\{\widetilde z_0\}}(\widetilde Z,\nu^*L)$. The degree is thus computed after strict localization, and the trait transition is applied to $\nu^*i^!(K|_{T_{(\bar x)}})$.

The trait transition is the natural map furnished by [lem-per-prime-power-trait-residue-model]. Explicitly, if $S$ is wild inertia, $G$ tame inertia and $I_G$ the augmentation ideal of $\Lambda[[G]]$ as defined in that lemma, its supported-cohomology model is
$$F(M)=\bigl[M_s\longrightarrow M_{\bar\eta}^S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda[[G]]}(I_G,M_{\bar\eta}^S)\bigr]$$
in degrees $0,1,2$. For a topological generator $\sigma$ of $G$, the degree-two component of $M_{\bar\eta}(-1)\to F(M)[2]$ is
$$M_{\bar\eta}(-1)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{av}_S}M_{\bar\eta}^S(-1)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,M_{\bar\eta}^S)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_\sigma}M_{\bar\eta}^S\xrightarrow{(\operatorname{ev}_{1-\sigma})^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Lambda[[G]]}(I_G,M_{\bar\eta}^S).$$
The continuous Hom uses the underlying additive group without an equivariance condition. The cited trait lemma supplies invertibility of the last evaluation, the comparison $F(\nu^*L)\simeq R\Gamma_{\{\widetilde z_0\}}(\widetilde Z,\nu^*L)$, and independence of the generator and representing complex after termwise application and totalization. A morphism of pinned complexes is a derived-category morphism whose induced maps on every $R\Gamma_x$ respect $p_x$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N4-d44dd9f7f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Re-delivery of the b41004 RETURN. I read in full the item, both new nodes, all 18 stmt_dep statements, the F_ell siblings and the 8 citers. I checked them against ILO XVII pp. 258-263: Def 1.1.1 with footnotes, 1.1.2, §1.2 (Props 1.2.1.2 and 1.2.2.1 with proof, 1.2.3, Lemma 1.2.3.2 with proof), §1.3, Defs 1.3.1, 1.4.1 and 2.1.1-2.1.2. All three return points are fixed. (1) D5: the inline claims now come from two real Z/ell^n lemmas. lem-per-prime-power-trait-residue-model covers 1.2.1.2, 1.2.2.1 and 1.2.3.2. lem-per-prime-power-costalk-reduction covers 1.1.1, 1.3 and 1.4.1. (2) B3: the notion citations are added, and stmt_deps equal the cited ids. (3) E5: the transition is now d^{-1} sp(nu^*i^!K) with d taken at the strict-local closed points. The evaluation order is ev_sigma then (ev_{1-sigma})^{-1}. The target Lambda(delta(y))[2delta(y)] is stated. The base definition is kept and not weakened. Small-case checks over Z/ell^n: (1-sigma): A -> I is an isomorphism. The finite-level kernel is the norm element, which dies in the limit because G has a Z_ell factor; surjectivity follows from Mittag-Leffler. F is exact (S is pro-p, p a unit mod ell^n). For the constant sheaf, F = [Lambda -id-> Lambda -0-> Hom(I,Lambda)], so H^2 = Lambda, matching Lambda(-1)[-2]. A sheaf supported at s gives sp = 0. Hom_cont(G,N) = Hom(mu_{ell^n},N). The p-power degree of the residue extension is a unit. The characteristic-0 and already-normal cases give d = 1. At n = 1 both new nodes are word for word the F_ell siblings, so the reviewed lem-per-potential-local-duality claim (at r=1 this definition is def-per-potential-dualizing) still holds. No duplicates in DAG-wide or live searches. The new nodes generalize the F_ell nodes and do not restate a parent clause. Blueprint from/via are correct. No SGA, no proof steps, no tool_uses. The live item is still unsplit. Maintainer note: the F_ell lem-per-trait-residue-model and lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction can be obtained by specializing the new nodes to n = 1. No fixes.
